name: Drekk IronPalm Weld & Chem Work Gauntlet
description:
Heavy-duty gauntlets built for the forge floor and acid-wash bays. Outer shell is heat-scored syn-leather over a nitrile-composite palm, stained amber and grey from sustained chemical exposure. Knuckle ridges are reinforced with stamped recycled ferrosteel plates. The wrist cuff is wide and buckled — designed to seal over jumpsuit sleeves or bare skin alike.

Cutaway index and middle fingers on the dominant hand allow for basic touchpad input without removal. Interior lining is moisture-wicking mesh, replaceable as a separate insert sold by the sheet at most Tier 1–2 hardware stalls.
functionality: Rated for temperatures up to 480°C brief contact. Chemical resistance against common industrial acids and solvents. Reinforced palm reduces vibration fatigue from pneumatic tools. Cutaway fingers allow limited terminal input without full removal.
what_it_says: You work with your hands in places that would ruin someone else's skin, and you don't expect anyone to thank you for it.
story_hooks: A pair of these gloves is found at a chemical spill scene — one glove missing, the other stiff with dried blood and something that isn't acid.
A Tier 2 factory rep is quietly selling counterfeit Drekk gauntlets rated for conditions they can't handle — three workers have already been burned.
The wearer's left gauntlet has a serial number that matches a pair reported stolen from a sealed hazmat site two years ago.

physical_description.visual_profile: Industrial gauntlet with a brutalist aesthetic—imposing hand armor that extends well past the wrist with a fortress-like silhouette. Worn-in patina suggests heavy labor on the factory floor. The cutaway fingers break the otherwise total enclosure, creating an asymmetrical, functional design statement.
physical_description.fit: Compression fit through the palm and fingers, relaxed and adjustable at the wide wrist cuff. Designed to accommodate both gloved and bare-armed workers; cuff sits snug over or under sleeve.
physical_description.primary_material: Heat-scored syn-leather shell over reinforced nitrile-composite palm; stamped recycled ferrosteel knuckle plates; moisture-wicking mesh interior lining (replaceable).
physical_description.texture: Rough, scarred leather surface with chemical staining; rigid, geometric knuckle ridges; tactile weave of interior mesh visible at cuff opening.
physical_description.color_scheme: Dominant amber and grey with deep charcoal shadows in creases. Ferrosteel plates show dull metallic gunmetal. Discoloration patterns map the wear history of acid and heat exposure.
physical_description.closures: Single heavy-duty buckle at wrist cuff; friction-fit seal mechanism designed to lock over fabric or skin.
distinctive_features: Cutaway index and middle fingers on dominant hand for touchpad/interface access
Weathered acid-stain pattern across palms and knuckles
Wide adjustable wrist cuff with locking buckle
Drekk Industrial Supply branding subtle on cuff edge
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3–4 functional workwear; tool-grade rather than luxury, but built to last and widely accessible on the industrial market.
physical_description.cultural_context: Signals skilled manufacturing labor, hazmat environment exposure, and street-level technical competence. Worn by forge workers, chem techs, salvage yards operators, and off-grid fabricators. Also adopted by Tier 5 sub-grade workers who source them secondhand.
physical_description.condition_typical: Heavily patched and weathered, with visible scars, discoloration, and embedded chemical stains. New pairs look pristine amber-grey; age brings darker mottling and micro-fractures in the leather.
